equivalent: EVEN IN p, BIT FOR BIT. p reaches the result only as p*p (both denominators) and as re_plus = p/d_plus and re_minus = p/d_minus, which are used only inside (re_plus - re_minus).powi(2). Under p -> -p: IEEE multiplication is exactly sign-symmetric so p*p is bit-identical, hence d_plus, d_minus, im_plus and im_minus are untouched; division negates the quotient exactly, so re_plus and re_minus each negate exactly and their difference negates exactly; powi(2) of a negated value is bit-identical. The returned f64 is therefore identical in every bit, not merely to rounding, so no assertion on the returned value could separate the two. Fixture built and both versions run side by side over 424,800 triples (b in [-21.83, 0] step 0.37, omega in [0.91, 53.7] step 0.91, omega_in in [0, 63.1] step 0.53): 0 of 424,800 differed in any bit. Edges checked too: b = +0.0 vs -0.0 (p = -0.0 vs +0.0) agree; the pole b = 0 driven exactly at omega gives NaN on both sides; b = -1e300 with omega = 1e300 gives 0.0 on both sides. What is NOT claimed: that p = b is as READABLE as p = -b, only that the function cannot distinguish them.
